elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: § 21.1 as rendered: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed ... The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims." Pre-existing and retained verbatim.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: § 21.1 now reads "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000." Uses lowercase "fees" and expressly reaches all Order Forms, so the illusory defined term "Fees" (USD 12,000 Implementation Fee) no longer governs; the USD 1,000,000 floor independently guarantees a meaningful cap.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: § 21.2 retained: "neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill."

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: § 21.3 Excluded Claims (outside the § 21.1 cap by "Except for Excluded Claims") includes "a Party's breach of confidentiality ... obligations."

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: § 21.3: "breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations" is an Excluded Claim and thus outside the cap.
§ 21.3: "its indemnification obligations" listed among Excluded Claims.
§ 21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" listed among Excluded Claims.
§ 21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" listed among Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: § 21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" listed among Excluded Claims.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: § 21.3 as rendered: "Customer's obligation to pay amounts due under this Agreement and any Order Form is not damages and is not limited by this Section." This cures the prior tie to the narrow defined term "Fees" (Implementation Fee only), so Customer payment obligations as a whole sit outside the cap.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: § 21.1: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... The cap is mutual."

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: § 21.1: "fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" (with a USD 1,000,000 floor).

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: § 21.3 Excluded Claims: "a Party's breach of confidentiality ... obligations."

reasons: Finding status "deviation" is correct: the pre-edit cap measured against "Fees" (defined at §§ 1.5-1.6 as the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form) is illusory and sits below the walk-away line, so neither the preferred nor the fallback cap basis was met before the edit.

Element coverage is complete at the preferred level after the edit; the § 21.1 reset (lowercase "fees", all Order Forms, greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor) properly escapes the illusory defined term, and § 21.3 now reaches Customer payment obligations as a whole.

Minimality fails at § 21.3: the edit deleted the Customer-favourable qualifiers "undisputed" and "for conforming Services" from the payment carve-out. Only the narrow "Fees" basis needed repair; stripping those limiters expands Customer's uncapped exposure to disputed amounts and to amounts charged for non-conforming Services, which is beyond the checklist element and removes favourable retained language. Repair: render § 21.3 as "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed amounts due for conforming Services under this Agreement and any Order Form is not damages and is not limited by this Section."

Secondary minimality note: § 21.1 also dropped the existing temporal anchor "the event giving rise to the claim" in favour of "the claim". The checklist element is literally "preceding the claim", so the element is met, but the original anchor was at least as protective and could have been retained ("the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim") without affecting element coverage.

Intent is preserved: the mutuality sentence, the mutual § 21.2 exclusion, the direct-damages sentence and the full Excluded Claims list survive unchanged; no dangling cross-reference or undefined trigger is created. One drafting hygiene point to confirm: § 21.1 now uses lowercase "fees" while "Fees" remains defined as the Implementation Fee — consider "all fees (including subscription and service fees, however denominated)" to foreclose an argument that the defined term controls.
